unsupported.label: Hasbro Pulse (direct)
unsupported.reason: The storefront is a client rendered single page app, so listings do not exist in the HTML that is served, and what sits behind it is a private commerce API rather than a public feed.
unsupported.coveredVia: Entertainment Earth carries these lines, so they do appear on the radar.

unsupported.label: NECA (direct)
unsupported.reason: necaonline.com/robots.txt disallows /products/ and /productlist/ for every crawler, which is where the listings live.
unsupported.coveredVia: Entertainment Earth lists NECA, so those products still reach the radar.

unsupported.label: McFarlane Toys (direct)
unsupported.reason: The site is a marketing showcase with no server rendered product data, no prices, and a sitemap that returns 404.
unsupported.coveredVia: Entertainment Earth lists McFarlane, so those products still reach the radar.

unsupported.label: Sideshow and Hot Toys
unsupported.reason: Every request is redirected into a virtual waiting room queue before a page is served. Working around that would mean evading a system built to control traffic.

unsupported.label: Medicom (direct)
unsupported.reason: The Medicom store publishes no product sitemap and its product endpoint returns nothing, so there is no listing to read.
unsupported.coveredVia: MAFEX appears when a covered retailer lists it.

unsupported.label: BigBadToyStore (filtered views)
unsupported.reason: bigbadtoystore.com/robots.txt allows /Search but disallows /Search?* , and every sorted or filtered listing is a query string on that path. The single unparameterised listing is read instead, which is why BBTS contributes a small number of rows.
unsupported.coveredVia: The unfiltered BigBadToyStore listing is read.
